title: AI Tools Are Ideal for Scenario Planning
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Scenario planning has always been something leaders know they should do and almost never actually do, because it requires deep research, sustained dialogue, and long meetings with talented people. The piece's thesis is that LLMs have collapsed the cost of pressure-testing plans to the point where leaders who skip it now are choosing to be surprised. An LLM can compile the research a human would take weeks to produce, poke holes in a draft plan, surface assumptions it rests on, and generate scenarios that would never occur to the leader. Three prompting habits turn the tool from rubber stamp into useful thought partner: keep the conversation going (one prompt gets an average response, useful work happens across three or four follow-ups), beware of sycophancy (explicitly instruct the model to red-team the plan and take apart assumptions), and be unreasonable (ask for twenty ideas instead of one, push for scenarios you would never ask a colleague to generate). The closing holds the line: the LLM can accelerate research and multiply scenarios but deciding which deserve attention and resources is still the leader's job.
points: Large language models have collapsed the cost of scenario planning and pressure-testing to the point where leaders who skip it are now choosing to be surprised.
Three prompting habits turn LLMs from rubber stamps into useful thought partners: keep the conversation going, explicitly instruct red-teaming, and ask for unreasonably many ideas.
The LLM accelerates research and multiplies scenarios; deciding which deserve organisational attention and resources remains the leader's job.
quotes: Even the best laid plans can fail when leaders encounter situations they didn't expect.
Through Scenario Planning, leaders can account for a wide range of possible situations. They can pressure test their plans and make sure they aren't caught unaware or without a backup strategy.

Scenario Planning that provides a clear benefit has traditionally required deep research, robust dialogue, and intensive discussion of different possibilities by the organization's most talented people. But with the large language models of AI now available to leaders, scenario planning can be fast, inexpensive, and more thorough.
As leaders begin the planning process, they can ask LLMs to poke holes in it, to identify the underlying assumptions the strategy depends upon, and to reveal potential missteps.

Don't depend on a single prompt. When the LLM provides its output, push against it, probe the assumptions it makes, and dive deeper into the questions at hand. The most useful outputs seldom come in the model's first response.

By nature, LLMs are agreeable and seek to satisfy the user. When you're looking for critique, ask the model to be critical. Ask it to serve as a true red team partner, poking holes in every aspect of your plan.
LLMs produce volumes of ideas and content far beyond what would be reasonable to ask a human being. Don't limit yourself. Rather than ask for one idea, ask for 20.

Great Scenario Planning keeps human judgment at the center while using AI to accelerate the process and strengthen the output. As helpful as LLMs can be in researching, defining, and planning across scenarios, leaders need to decide which are worth their attention.” Archived from Admired Leadership Field Notes on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
